question: Step by step: enquiry source → first contact → survey visit → quote → follow-up → decision. Who does each step?
Typical numbers per firm per month: enquiries, surveys, quotes sent, jobs won. Close rate from quote to sale (hypothesis: 20-35%). Average job value (hypothesis: £3k-£15k).
How long does a homeowner take to decide? How long does an old quote stay "alive"? Is a 2-year-old quote worth chasing? A 5-year-old one?
Why do quotes die? Price, timing, bought elsewhere, never followed up, partner said no, finance refused, project postponed. Rough split?
How many follow-ups does a typical installer do after sending a quote? (Hypothesis: 0-2.)
Do they sell on the first visit ("sit and close") or send quotes and wait? The big nationals do the first; independents mostly the second. Affects the size of the backlog.
Where are old quotes stored: paper, Excel/Google Sheets, email inbox, quoting software, CRM?
What fields do they have per quote: name, phone, email, address, date, products, price, status, notes? Often phone but no email?
How many old quotes does a typical firm have (hypothesis: 500-5,000)?
What they currently spend on getting work: lead sites, ads, canvassing, showrooms, trade shows. Monthly budget.
What a booked survey is worth to them (job value × close rate × margin), so we know what we can charge.
Top objections and past burns: "tried agencies", "leads were rubbish", "my data's a mess", "I don't want to annoy old customers", "GDPR", "I'm too busy", "sounds too good".
Buying triggers: quiet month, lost a salesperson, new showroom, cash flow, seasonal dip.
Who decides and who influences: owner, co-owner/spouse, office manager, sales manager. How to reach the owner.
Which months are busy (spring/summer?) vs quiet (winter?). When are they most open to buying a service? When do homeowners buy windows?
Does reactivation work better at certain times (January "new year projects", before winter, energy bill spikes)?
Price per result that is a no-brainer for them and profitable for us: model it from job value, close rate and our delivery cost.
Does a free pilot attract the wrong clients or delay revenue? What converts pilots into paid?
What works on UK trade owners: length, tone (casual/direct), plain text vs formatting, spelling (British English), no jargon ("database reactivation" means nothing to them).
Subject lines that get opened by a busy owner, including lowercase/short/company-name styles.
First lines: which personalisation is real and valuable vs creepy/fake? What true data we have: years trading, town, FENSA/Certass, services on their site, reviews.
The call to action: ask for a call, ask a question, offer a free audit, ask for permission to send info. Which gets more positive replies?
Proof without case studies: how to be credible with zero clients (honest framing, the mechanism, a pilot offer).
Follow-ups: how many (3? 5?), gaps between them, what each one adds (new angle, maths, social proof, break-up).
Replying: templates for "how much?", "send info", "not interested", "who are you?", "how did you get my email?", "remove me", out-of-office.
Personalisation at scale: when AI-written first lines help and when they hurt.
Safe volume per inbox per day (hypothesis: 30-50) and ramp schedule.
Bounce handling: verify emails before sending? which verifier? What bounce rate is dangerous (hypothesis: >2%)?
Decision-maker first names: Companies House officers (directors) as a proxy for the owner; accuracy for small firms.
Email accuracy: generic inbox vs named; how often info@ reaches the owner in a small firm.
What are realistic numbers per 1,000 emails sent: delivered, replies, positive replies, calls booked, clients won?
How many leads do we need to hit 1, 5, 20 clients? We have 1,918 ranked + more if other niches.
What proof convinces installers most: £ recovered, surveys booked, a named local firm, a video testimonial?
Client-to-client referrals: incentive that works.
Timing: day/time for homeowners; gaps between messages; how many touches before stopping.
Realistic reply and booking rates from old quotes, by quote age (hypothesis: 5-15% reply, 2-5% booked).
How results decay with quote age and with repeated campaigns.

section: Part 9: Results, attribution and billing (V + C)
question: Per-client economics: time spent, SMS/tool costs, margin.
Why clients leave in this model (list exhausted, results drop, they stop answering leads) and how to prevent each.
Monthly value that justifies staying after month 1-2.
Unit economics per client: price, delivery costs (GHL, SMS, tools, our time), gross margin.
Cash flow on performance deals: costs we carry before we get paid; how long.
Cost to acquire a client (tools, domains, data, our time) and payback period.
Financial model: clients × price × retention → months to £30k and £100k.
What lift did the campaign cause versus what would have happened anyway? Use a holdout/control group when sample size permits, not only post-contact attribution.
What is the client’s pre-campaign organic reopen/close rate for the same quote-age cohorts?
Are booked/quoted/won results still valuable after cancellations, refunds, duplicate jobs and non-payment?
Can the installer actually handle the recovered survey/install volume in the relevant geography and weeks, or will success create a fulfillment bottleneck?
